structural_memory.memory: Cargo-tank pressure/vacuum relief and venting service spans owner/manager, master and deck/cargo team, engineering crew, shore technical or cargo support, relief/venting equipment or service actors and relevant terminal, port or yard support. Protective-path readiness, tank scope, monitoring and shore intervention should remain distinct roles rather than one valve-setting, test or operating directory.

Protective relief/vent path readiness is distinct from inert-gas source or supply readiness. An inert-gas service can be available while the protective relief/vent path is unavailable or uncertain, and a relief-path concern does not itself prove an inert-gas source failure.

Tank-scope or tank-interface confidence is distinct from common relief/vent path availability. A common protective path can appear available while one tank, tank group or bounded interface remains unavailable or uncertain.

Non-numeric pressure/vacuum protection confidence is a service outcome state rather than a retained set pressure, capacity or operating target. Structural memory can distinguish available, degraded, uncertain, restricted and restored protection without preserving adjustment guidance.

Monitoring or indication confidence is distinct from actual protective relief/vent readiness. An indication, alarm or local status can change confidence but does not by itself establish path condition, protection margin, root cause or required action.

Independence or support confidence is a separate dimension: protective relief/venting may depend on mechanical condition, sensing/indication or other bounded support while still needing independence from ordinary cargo-control functions. Support availability does not equal protective-service availability.

Protective-path condition can include bounded interface confidence around vent outlets or protective devices without retaining exact flame-device designs, valve settings, path geometry or maintenance/test details. Device-condition uncertainty should remain distinct from tank pressure/vacuum outcome confidence.

Redundancy or alternate protective-path confidence can exist at system or tank scope, but structural memory should not infer exact arrangements, cross-connections, capacities, approved substitutions or valve positions.

Pressure/vacuum-relief degradation follows a defensive lifecycle: observation, uncertain path/tank/interface/monitoring/support scope, affected-state identification, restriction or uncertainty, bounded isolation, restoration indication and post-restoration verification. No venting, valve-setting, testing or emergency procedure is retained.

Restriction or isolation should be scoped to the affected relief/vent path, tank or tank group, monitoring domain, support function or protective interface rather than generalized to the entire cargo system. Exact valve or device actions remain deferred.

Pressure/vacuum-relief degradation can propagate into cargo-operation restrictions, inert-gas or vapor-control confidence, environmental/safety assurance, terminal compatibility, rework or schedule, but those effects are not themselves proof of a relief-path, tank-interface, monitoring or support root cause.

Protective-service confidence can remain scope-specific even when cargo transfer is otherwise available. Transfer readiness, vapor-return readiness and relief/vent protection should not be collapsed into a single cargo-system healthy/unhealthy flag.

Restoration can have multiple timestamps: protective-path condition returns, tank/interface scope is re-established, monitoring/indication confidence is renewed, support/independence confidence is restored and the affected pressure/vacuum-protection scope is separately verified. One alarm reset or device-ready indication does not prove full restoration.

P091 inert-gas service concerns source/supply and blanket confidence, while P097 concerns distinct pressure/vacuum-relief and venting protection. Healthy inert-gas confidence does not equal relief-path readiness, and relief-path degradation does not prove inert-gas failure.

P093 cargo-vapor return/control concerns managed vapor-path and terminal-interface availability, while P097 concerns protective pressure/vacuum relief and venting. A vapor-return path can be available while protective relief confidence is degraded or uncertain.

P096 high-level/overfill assurance protects a different hazard pathway from P097 pressure/vacuum relief. Independent high-level detection and protective relief/vent readiness should remain separately represented even when both affect cargo-operation restrictions.

P067 equipment lifecycle concepts refine relief/vent-device condition and restoration, but an equipment lifecycle state does not equal delivered pressure/vacuum protective service across the intended tank scope.
Generic protective-equipment, path, monitoring, support and restoration mechanics overlap prior shipboard utility, equipment and cargo-protection passes.

Scoped degradation, restriction/isolation, downstream-effect separation and multi-stage restoration mechanics overlap prior shipboard service passes; P097 applies them specifically to cargo-tank pressure/vacuum relief and venting.

It is not valve-setting, testing, venting-operation, cargo-operation, emergency-response or vessel-operating advice and does not establish any exact arrangement, set pressure, capacity, valve setting, path, flame-device detail, control mode, alarm threshold, test result, procedure, provider, incident, deficiency finding or current-readiness fact.
stop_reason: Pressure/vacuum-relief and venting protective service is recalled at useful non-operational resolution: protective relief/vent path readiness, tank scope, non-numeric pressure/vacuum protection confidence, monitoring/indication confidence, independence/support confidence, scoped restriction/isolation and verified restoration are separable states. Further detail would become vessel-, tanker-type-, pressure-, vacuum-, capacity-, valve-, vent-, flame-device-, test-, procedure-, provider- or incident-specific and is deferred to claim-scoped Evidence.
